newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bright days ahead for Belgian Bel-20.
newsitem.headline: Bright days ahead for Belgian Bel-20.

text.p: The Bel-20 index, a string of all-time closing highs under its belt, is bound to cruise further into uncharted territory as the share market sees a further influx of funds being shifted from bonds, current accounts and bank savings certificates in 1997, analysts said.
"It should be a good year for the bourse," said Stefan Casteleyn at Antwerp brokerage Corluy & Co.
The Bel-20 jumped 1.30 percent, or 24.80 points, higher at a new closing high of 1929.62, the third record session this week.
"Low interest rates still have not been fully discounted," Casteleyn said.
The Brussels bourse, profiting from a morale-boosting cocktail of Dow and dollar strength, in-line U.S. PPI data and solid bonds, easily outperformed other European markets.
Some dealers did not exclude a technical correction on Friday but stressed the overall picture remained rosy.
Casteleyn said the German Bundesbank might be tempted to cut leading rates one more time in February or March if it became obvious that economic growth would continue to be curtailed.
"There will be growth, but limited, and it will not lead to extra jobs," he said.
He said that holdings were among the brokerage's favourites.
He said that holdings would gradually lose their discount this year, noting that GBL still stood at a discount of 26 percent and Almanij at about 20 percent.

Insurer Royale Belge was among the leading gainers with a 2.9 percent advance to 6,690 francs. Casteleyn said it had been standing too much in the shadow of fellow insurer Fortis AG, which has been climbing steadily and today again added 2.1 percent to 5,310.
"Royale Belge too is not bad at all," he said.
Retailer Colruyt was the biggest loser for most of the day before paring its losses to close 0.7 percent weaker at 13,900.
"It's difficult for Colruyt to announce any more real earnings surprises," said Casteleyn, noting it had been among Belgium's best performing stocks in the 1990s.

Colruyt said on Wednesday its first half 1996-1997 consolidated net profit rose 11.6 percent to 1.105 billion Belgian francs from 990 million in the same year-ago period. The rise was broadly in line with analysts' expectations.
